summary: Chicago's guidewall light at the Chicago River lock: its tower was built for Kewaunee, Wisconsin, in 1912 and installed here in 1938.

structures.note: Built 1912 as the Kewaunee Pierhead tower, 45 ft tall; installed at the Chicago guidewall in 1938. The record's 9.0 m is not in the sources read.

access.note: Tower closed; fairly good views from the south side of Navy Pier (LighthouseFriends).

events.note: Tower built for the Kewaunee Pierhead light, Wisconsin; first exhibited night of 26 Mar 1912. Not this site.
Railroad carferry struck the south pier at Kewaunee and twisted one tower support leg. Kewaunee tower, not this site.
Tower sailed from Kewaunee to Milwaukee, 27 May 1932; slight damage repaired at the Milwaukee Lighthouse Depot.
Chicago River locks and guidewalls built between 1936 and 1938 (LighthouseFriends); the Illinois DNR gives completion of the lock in 1938.
Tower installed in Chicago as the Chicago Harbor Southeast Guidewall Lighthouse, at the eastern end of the guidewall.
Light described in 1938 as occulting (LighthouseFriends, original 1938 description not traced).

corrections.why: 1912 is the year the tower was built for the Kewaunee Pierhead light, Wisconsin. The tower was installed at this site in 1938 (Kewaunee Pierhead Lighthouse history; LighthouseFriends).

resolved_conflicts.field: first light at the river mouth (1832 or 1833)
resolved_conflicts.explanation: The 1937 Lighthouse Service review gives 1832 for the first lighthouse placed at the mouth of the Chicago River; LighthouseFriends gives 1833 for the first Chicago light near the mouth. The story gives both.
LighthouseFriends dates the tower's Kewaunee service 1912 to 1931; the Kewaunee history has it stored at the pier until it was sailed to Milwaukee on 27 May 1932. The story gives both.
The 1912 date is the tower's first life at Kewaunee, where it was first exhibited 26 March 1912; it reached Chicago in 1938. The guidewall station's own date is 1938.

LighthouseFriends ties the lock to a 1930 Supreme Court order and says it was built 1936-1938; the Illinois DNR says a 1933 decree ordered the lock and that it was completed in 1938. The story gives both dates with their sources.

notes_for_editor: Roster: roster.py matched CHICAGO HARBOR (USLHS nid 2803, 155 roster lines, 1893-1976), which is the 1893 breakwater light, not this guidewall; it is not used. The other candidate, Chicago Harbor (Fort Dearborn), is a discontinued 1833-1859 light. A USLHS minor-aid record, Chicago Harbor South Entrance, exists (Existing: Yes; Open to Public: No; no other fields), but it is not confirmed as this light. No keeper is named for this light in the sources read. LighthouseFriends prints keeper lists on this page (Thomas J. Bailey 1906-09 onward); they are for the older Chicago harbor and pierhead lights and are not linked here, so the keepers list is empty. Record visit.boat_only is true; LighthouseFriends' visitor notes describe views from Navy Pier, and the record was not changed. Record structure height 9.0 m is unsourced; the Kewaunee tower was 45 ft when built. Record characteristic Iso W 6s (ENC) differs from the 1938 description as occulting (LighthouseFriends, quoting an untraced 1938 source); a characteristic change may be unrecorded. Not verified: current characteristic and height. The Lighthouse Board volumes after 1901 are not in the corpus; no Lighthouse Service Bulletin text about this light in 1938-39 was found. The 1930 Supreme Court date rests on LighthouseFriends; a 1930 New York Times headline was seen in search results but not read. Britannica returned 403.
